Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Ulvi\Desktop\bank-cs-agent-builder\kit\build-the-builder\.claude\skills\build-phone-agent

# Build a phone agent from a brief

Work from the kit folder. Use only what the brief and the tool API file say. Do not copy rules from another brief.

## Steps

1. Read `README.md`, `VERSION`, the brief files, the exact OpenAPI file named in the request, and `../../builder/learned-questions.md`.
2. Discover the platform documentation fresh on every run with `Glob docs/**/*`. Read every relevant current document; do not assume document names or rely on a remembered Freya schema. Treat the current starter-kit metadata, discovered docs and exact OpenAPI file as the source of truth for this run.
3. Read `examples/base-agent.json`. It is a small working agent with two steps. Use it as the pattern for the JSON, not as the answer.
4. Write the workflow to `out/<slot>.workflow.json`. `<slot>` is the brief's file name without `.md`. Do not read an existing file for this slot before the first write; rebuild it blind from the inputs.
   - One step per stage of the call. Identity comes first.
   - Move to the next step on a tool result, not on what the customer says.
   - Take every tool field and allowed value from the exact OpenAPI file named in the request.
   - Leave `agent_config` out.
5. Before preflight, perform at most two requirement-coverage passes with the same stateful agent:
   - Pass one: reread the brief and OpenAPI, make a requirement-to-workflow ledger covering every mandatory rule, table row, amendment, exception, tool outcome, retry and terminal path, then fix every omission in the existing JSON.
   - Pass two: reread the source independently of the first conclusion, verify the ledger mappings and every changed area, and fix any remaining omission. Stop after this pass even if uncertain.
   Do not regenerate the JSON and do not start an open-ended review loop. Then run `python ../../builder/preflight.py out/<slot>.workflow.json <the-exact-openapi-path>`, fix every ERROR, review WARN lines against the brief, and dry-run with `freya.validate_workflow`.
6. Save it: `python3 -c "import freya,json,sys; print(json.dumps(freya.save_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2])), state_file='../../.freya-agents.json')))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json`
   It prints `workflow_id` and `agent_id`. The same slot updates the same workflow.
7. If the request names a practice label, test it with an output file: `python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --brief <label> --out results/<slot>-run<N>.json`. A run takes 3 to 11 minutes. Run it in the foreground and wait for it to finish. Never start it in the background and never end your turn while a test is running. If there are no matching practice customers, do not test against A or B.
8. On failure, run `python ../../builder/analyze_results.py results/<slot>-run<N>.json`. Read the evidence file. Change only the workflow part supported by ledger, policy, honesty, transcript, tool or route evidence. Save and retest only failed cases when useful. Do this at most three times.
9. Do not use `--reps` inside a builder run. One full practice run plus targeted failed-case retests must fit the build budget; repeated durability validation is a separate operation.
10. If an evidence-supported edit taught a reusable lesson, distill it into exactly one brief-independent question and append it to `../../builder/learned-questions.md`. Preserve the failure pattern, never the instance: do not include dates, amounts, case ids, outcome names, customer names or expected answers.
11. Finish with one line: the `workflow_id`, the `agent_id` and how many customers passed in the last run. Leave enough time for the caller to export the saved workflow and finish the trace.

## Rules

- Never edit the agent on the platform by hand. Change the file and save it.
- Before the first save, do not read `public-test-set.json`, old `results`, traces or practice customer definitions. Build blind from the brief, OpenAPI and platform docs. Practice evidence is for fixing after the first test.
- If the brief defines calendar, deadline or date-normalization rules, first extract the policy from whatever form the brief uses, including prose, tables, mails and amendments, then compile that policy into deterministic code. Do not assume a fixed precedence between date signals: follow precedence stated by the brief, and ask for clarification rather than discard conflicting components when the brief is silent. Return structured `normalized`, `valid`, `replacement` and `reason` values; do not ask the dialogue model to calculate dates.
- Validate a date before read-back and confirmation. A write-tool pre-hook may reject an invalid confirmed value, but must never silently replace it with a different date after the customer confirmed it; route back for a new read-back instead.
- When limits, attempts or dispositions apply per item, keep `attempts_allowed`, `attempts_used`, offers made and terminal disposition in deterministic per-item state. Compute the next permitted action from that state; do not ask the dialogue model to count attempts from conversation history. Once an item reaches a terminal disposition, exclude it from later offers.
- When a tool call fails, the agent must say so. It must never tell the customer something is recorded when it is not.
- A customer that passes once can fail the next time. Prefer rules in routes and code over rules in prompts.
- When a read returns several items, verify that every item reaches exactly one disposition allowed by the brief before the call closes, unless a transfer replaces item-level writes.

# Build the Builder

**Kit version 3** (10 October 2026). The file `VERSION` holds the number. When we update the kit, the number goes up and the changes are listed here.

- v3: the example builder waits for its own test run (up to 20 minutes per command) instead of stopping before the results arrive. On Brief A it built an agent that passed 10 of the 10 practice customers in one run.
- v2: `examples/base-agent.json` (an example phone agent) and `examples/agent_builder.py` with the skill `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent` (an example builder) replace `examples/minimal_builder.py`.
- v1: first release.

You write a **builder**: a program that reads a bank's brief and creates a phone agent on Freya.
We put that phone agent in front of simulated customers. The share it handles correctly is your score.

One simulated customer is one case. A step of a phone agent is called a node in the platform's documents.

## The ten-minute start

You need Python 3.10 or newer.

```bash
cp env.example env.sh        # put your Freya API key in it, and a team key you make up
source env.sh

# 1. Put the example agent on Freya and test it. It prints {"workflow_id": ..., "agent_id": ...}
python3 -c "import freya,json; print(freya.save_workflow('base', json.load(open('examples/base-agent.json'))))"
python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --brief A            # ten practice customers, 3 to 11 minutes

# 2. Let the example builder build one from the brief
pip install claude-agent-sdk
python3 examples/agent_builder.py briefs/brief-a.md
python3 examples/agent_builder.py briefs/brief-a.md briefs/brief-b.md   # Brief B builds on Brief A, so pass both
```

`run_cases.py` prints one line per customer: pass or fail, the tool calls the agent made, and the reason for a failure.

`examples/base-agent.json` is an agent, not a builder. It is the same two-step workflow that is already in your workspace: check identity, then take a payment promise. It uses four of the seven tools, so it handles only the simplest customers: in one run it passed 2 of the 13 practice customers. Read it to see what a valid workflow looks like.

`examples/agent_builder.py` is a builder. It runs Claude through the Claude Agent SDK with one skill, `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent/SKILL.md`. Claude reads the brief and the tool API file, writes the workflow, runs the practice customers and fixes what fails. The skill is short on purpose. Your job is a better builder: a better skill, more skills, your own code, or another agent altogether. It needs a Claude login or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## What is in this kit

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `briefs/brief-a.md` | Freya Bank's specification for customers late on one product. 47 rules. Read all of it. |
| `briefs/brief-b.md` | The extra rules for customers with up to three products. It builds on Brief A. |
| `tools/openapi.json` | The bank's tool API that the phone agent calls during a call. |
| `public-test-set.json` | 13 practice customers: what each one does and what the bank's records must show afterwards. |
| `examples/base-agent.json` | An example phone agent: two steps, four tools. The same one that is in your workspace. |
| `examples/agent_builder.py` | An example builder on the Claude Agent SDK. Claude builds, tests and fixes the agent. |
| `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent/SKILL.md` | The one skill the example builder uses. |
| `freya.py` | A small client for the Freya API. Standard library only. |
| `tools/run_cases.py`, `tools/score.py` | Run the practice customers against a phone agent and score it. |
| `docs/workflow-format.md` | What a phone agent is made of: steps, prompts, variables, routes. |
| `docs/tools-and-code.md` | Tools that call an API, code steps, hooks, where a tool's response lands. |
| `docs/api.md` | The API calls a builder needs. |

## How you are scored

A customer counts as handled when all of these hold:

1. **Outcome: the bank's records are right.** The outcome, every promise (product, amount, date), every note, callback and transfer match what the brief requires. The scorer reads them from the bank, not from what the agent said.
2. **Policy: the conversation stayed inside the brief.**
3. **Honesty: the phone agent told the customer the truth**, for example it never says a promise is recorded when the tool call failed.

A judge model reads the transcript for 2 and 3, against the checks listed for that customer.

There is no partial credit. Your score is the share of customers handled.

The same phone agent can pass a customer in one run and fail it in the next. Treat one green run as a hint, not as proof.

## The final

- On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. They are the same kind of call with different rules: other numbers and limits, other identity questions, another outcome table, another calendar. Their form can differ too: one final brief is a clean specification, the other is raw bank material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo that changes it, a code list).
- Each final brief comes with its own tool API file. The seven tool names stay the same. The fields and the allowed values can change.
- After the final briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a final brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
- You run your builder once on each, with no manual step, and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
- You export each phone agent to a file with `freya.export_workflow(workflow_id, "<brief>.workflow.json")` and submit those files. We load them into our own workspace to test them, so what you export is what we score.
- We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen, on several calendar days, three times each. A customer counts only when all three runs pass. A phone agent that is right most of the time is not right.
- Final customers can have up to three products, as in Brief B.
- Final customers talk like people. They give a number in two parts, correct themselves, talk about other things, ask a question back, or say amounts and dates in words. The facts stay the same. Practise with `--style pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words` on `run_cases.py`.

So build something that reads a brief, not something that knows this one. Whatever your builder can take from the brief, it should take from the brief.

## Rules

- Your builder takes brief files as input and creates the phone agent with no manual step. Do not edit a phone agent by hand after it is created.
- The phone agent runs on the model set in `freya.py` (`AGENT_LLM`). Do not change it. Your builder may use any model or coding agent.
- The phone agent may call only the bank's tool API. Code steps and hooks inside the workflow are allowed and expected.
- Use `freya.save_workflow(...)` or update your workflow in place. A workspace holds 200 workflows. A builder that creates a new one on every run fills it up and leaves you with a list nobody can read.
- One simulation runs at a time per workspace. A ten-customer run takes 3 to 11 minutes. A second `run_cases.py` started meanwhile waits for the first.
- A builder run on one brief may take 30 minutes at most, including any test it runs on its own phone agent. You may run it more than once and submit the phone agent of one run, with that run's trace.
- Equal scores are ranked by the total promised amount on the customers that passed, then by shorter build time, then by earlier submission.
- Your builder must leave a trace of each run: start and end time, each model call it made (model and a one-line purpose), what it created on Freya, and any test it ran on its own agent. Plain text, no fixed format. You submit one trace per final brief.
- All data here is synthetic. Do not bring real customer data.

## When something does not work

- `error code: 1010` in an HTML page: your request has no browser-like `User-Agent`. `freya.py` sets one.
- `Workspace plan limit reached`: you created too many workflows. Update one in place.
- You changed your builder and the score did not move at all: an updated workflow must be published before a simulation uses it. `freya.save_workflow` publishes. A plain `PUT` does not. See "Update a workflow" in `docs/api.md`.
- A customer fails and you do not see why: `freya.get_call(call_id)["messages"]` is the full transcript with the tool calls. `run_cases.py --out results/run.json` saves the call id of every customer.
- Calls end as `customer-ended-call` before the phone agent is done: it was silent too long and the customer hung up, as a person would. `run_cases.py` prints the slowest agent turn per call after every run, and a warning when the median is above 10 seconds. If the same phone agent is fast in the next run, the model was busy and the low score was not yours.
- You want to see what your phone agent says without waiting for a simulation: `POST /api/v2/chat/message` runs one turn at a time. See `docs/api.md`.
- The bank answers `unknown product_id`: the model made an id up. Product ids come from `get_account` (`p1`, `p2`, ...). Give them to the model in the tool result, or fill them in with code.
- A simulation stays at "running" and no call ever starts: the workflow cannot start a call. Try one chat turn. Leave `agent_config` out of the workflow you send.
- The agent says nothing after a tool call and the customer hangs up: see "Tool results and the next turn" in `docs/tools-and-code.md`.

# Learned questions

- Does every spoken `{{variable}}` have a producer that runs before that node, or is it explicitly supplied as a call input?
- Could wording required for a disclosure be mistaken by the judge for a claim that a write tool already succeeded?
- When a read returns several items, does every item reach exactly one brief-defined terminal disposition before closing, except when the brief says a transfer replaces item-level writes?
- When the brief defines calendar rules, is every customer-proposed date normalized and validated by deterministic code before any offer or write?
- Does code that reads an engine-run call's result look it up under the node-named flattened keys (not only the tool name or a response mapping), and was it tested against that exact key shape?
- When items carry different limits, does the agent check a customer-proposed value against each item's own limit and preserve it wherever it is valid?
- When an utterance contains multiple date signals, does deterministic code follow the brief-defined precedence or request clarification instead of silently discarding one?
- Can any write-tool hook silently change a value after the customer confirmed it, instead of rejecting it and requiring a new read-back?
- Does every conversation node where the customer can first answer a question (not only the main negotiation node) extract the values that deterministic checks read, and does each API tool's pre-hook rebuild a well-formed request when the model sends flat arguments, with terminal routing allowing one retry after a failed close?
- Does code that reads a model-filled tool argument look it up under the placeholder variable name used in the field's default (not only the API field name), with a fallback scan of all argument keys?
- When limits or attempts differ by item, does deterministic per-item state compute the next allowed action and permanently exclude items that already reached a terminal disposition?
- When code rebuilds an API result from the engine's flattened result keys (because a whole-body mapping did not land), does it turn numeric-index keys back into lists, and was it checked against a real call's variable table?

A customer counts as handled when all of these hold:

1. **Outcome: the bank's records are right.** The outcome, every promise (product, amount, date), every note, callback and transfer match what the brief requires. The scorer reads them from the bank, not from what the agent said.
2. **Policy: the conversation stayed inside the brief.**
3. **Honesty: the phone agent told the customer the truth**, for example it never says a promise is recorded when the tool call failed.

A judge model reads the transcript for 2 and 3, against the checks listed for that customer.

There is no partial credit. Your score is the share of customers handled.

The same phone agent can pass a customer in one run and fail it in the next. Treat one green run as a hint, not as proof.

## The final

- On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. They are the same kind of call with different rules: other numbers and limits, other identity questions, another outcome table, another calendar. Their form can differ too: one final brief is a clean specification, the other is raw bank material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo that changes it, a code list).
- Each final brief comes with its own tool API file. The seven tool names stay the same. The fields and the allowed values can change.
- After the final briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a final brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
- You run your builder once on each, with no manual step, and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
- You export each phone agent to a file with `freya.export_workflow(workflow_id, "<brief>.workflow.json")` and submit those files. We load them into our own workspace to test them, so what you export is what we score.
- We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen, on several calendar days, three times each. A customer counts only when all three runs pass. A phone agent that is right most of the time is not right.
- Final customers can have up to three products, as in Brief B.
- Final customers talk like people. They give a number in two parts, correct themselves, talk about other things, ask a question back, or say amounts and dates in words. The facts stay the same. Practise with `--style pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words` on `run_cases.py`.

So build something that reads a brief, not something that knows this one. Whatever your builder can take from the brief, it should take from the brief.

## Rules

- Your builder takes brief files as input and creates the phone agent with no manual step. Do not edit a phone agent by hand after it is created.
- The phone agent runs on the model set in `freya.py` (`AGENT_LLM`). Do not change it. Your builder may use any model or coding agent.
- The phone agent may call only the bank's tool API. Code steps and hooks inside the workflow are allowed and expected.
- Use `freya.save_workflow(...)` or update your workflow in place. A workspace holds 200 workflows. A builder that creates a new one on every run fills it up and leaves you with a list nobody can read.
- One simulation runs at a time per workspace. A ten-customer run takes 3 to 11 minutes. A second `run_cases.py` started meanwhile waits for the first.
- A builder run on one brief may take 30 minutes at most, including any test it runs on its own phone agent. You may run it more than once and submit the phone agent of one run, with that run's trace.
- Equal scores are ranked by the total promised amount on the customers that passed, then by shorter build time, then by earlier submission.
- Your builder must leave a trace of each run: start and end time, each model call it made (model and a one-line purpose), what it created on Freya, and any test it ran on its own agent. Plain text, no fixed format. You submit one trace per final brief.
- All data here is synthetic. Do not bring real customer data.

## When something does not work

- `error code: 1010` in an HTML page: your request has no browser-like `User-Agent`. `freya.py` sets one.
- `Workspace plan limit reached`: you created too many workflows. Update one in place.
- You changed your builder and the score did not move at all: an updated workflow must be published before a simulation uses it. `freya.save_workflow` publishes. A plain `PUT` does not. See "Update a workflow" in `docs/api.md`.
- A customer fails and you do not see why: `freya.get_call(call_id)["messages"]` is the full transcript with the tool calls. `run_cases.py --out results/run.json` saves the call id of every customer.
- Calls end as `customer-ended-call` before the phone agent is done: it was silent too long and the customer hung up, as a person would. `run_cases.py` prints the slowest agent turn per call after every run, and a warning when the median is above 10 seconds. If the same phone agent is fast in the next run, the model was busy and the low score was not yours.
- You want to see what your phone agent says without waiting for a simulation: `POST /api/v2/chat/message` runs one turn at a time. See `docs/api.md`.
- The bank answers `unknown product_id`: the model made an id up. Product ids come from `get_account` (`p1`, `p2`, ...). Give them to the model in the tool result, or fill them in with code.
- A simulation stays at "running" and no call ever starts: the workflow cannot start a call. Try one chat turn. Leave `agent_config` out of the workflow you send.
- The agent says nothing after a tool call and the customer hangs up: see "Tool results and the next turn" in `docs/tools-and-code.md`.

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract

Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
Date: 1 October 2026
Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)

> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.

## 1. Before you start

- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
- Base address for all seven:

```
https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
```

  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).

## 2. Access token

The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.

```
POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
```

Answer:

```json
{
  "access_token": "<token>",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 1800
}
```

Then on every service call:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
| `Accept` | `application/json` |

The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.

(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)

## 3. Envelope

### Request

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.

### Response

Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.

```json
{
  "data": { "...service fields..." },
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
    "returnCode": "1",
    "messageText": "Success",
    "code": "1",
    "message": "Success",
    "type": null,
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
      "rootCause": null,
      "errorOrigin": null
    }
  }
}
```

Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.

## 4. Errors

Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "code": "FBE00099",
    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
    "type": "ERROR",
    "details": {
      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
    }
  }
}
```

`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.

Codes you can get:

| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |

Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.

Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.

## 5. Services

| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |
| 5.2 | `cards.balance` | card number | statement and due dates, debt per currency |
| 5.3 | `statement.week.get` | card number | the card's current statement week and day, joint statement info |
| 5.4 | `statement.week.decide` | card number + requested week | what the dates *would* be with that week (does not change anything) |
| 5.5 | `statement.week.change` | card number + requested week | changes the statement week |
| 5.6 | `contact.email.get` | customer number | registered e-mail / phone |
| 5.7 | `statement.pdf.send` | customer, card, currency, statement date, address | sends the statement PDF by e-mail |

Card number: always send the `cardNumber` **exactly as `cards.list` returned it**. Don't rebuild it from digits the caller says.

### 5.1 `cards.list`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "customerNo": "90000001", "aiFlow": "CardOps" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

`customerNo` may be sent as a string or as a number, both are accepted. `aiFlow` tells us which use case is asking; for this one it's `"CardOps"` (not validated in test).

Response, one card:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cards": [
      {
        "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
        "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
        "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
        "status": "A",
        "isMainCard": true
      }
    ],
    "validCardsCount": 1,
    "exitState": "1_CARD"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "as in section 3" }
}
```

Response, several cards (abridged):

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cards": [
      { "cardNumber": "540000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "545000******4253", "cardNumberLast4": "4253", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "540000******6184", "cardNumberLast4": "6184", "productName": "Yıldız Pratik", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true },
      { "cardNumber": "540000******8870", "cardNumberLast4": "8870", "productName": "Yıldız Tasarım", "status": "A", "isMainCard": true }
    ],
    "validCardsCount": 4,
    "exitState": "MULTI_CARD"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

- `exitState`: `"1_CARD"` or `"MULTI_CARD"`.
- Only active cards come back (`status` `"A"`). `isMainCard` is `false` for a card that isn't the customer's own main card; it's still in the list.
- Two cards can have the same product name and the same last four digits (see above). Don't assume `cardNumberLast4` is unique.
- `productName` is free text from the card system, whatever was typed in there.
- Masking: in the **test environment** `cardNumber` comes back masked, first 6 and last 4 digits visible (`540000******1234`). What production returns in this field I still have to confirm with the card platform team; build so that it works with the masked form.

Errors: 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102`, 500 `FBE00099`.

### 5.2 `cards.balance`

Request:

```json
{
  "data": { "cardNumber": "540000******1234" },
  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "cardNumber": "5400********1234",
    "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
    "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
    "statementDate": "05.10.2026",
    "lastPayDate": "15.10.2026",
    "nextStatementDate": "05.11.2026",
    "nextLastPayDate": "15.11.2026",
    "debtTL": {
      "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
      "transferAmount": 0.0,
      "statementDebt": 5000.13,
      "minPayment": 2000.05,
      "remainingDebt": 5000.13,
      "remainingMinPayment": 2000.05,
      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
      "totalDebt": 5000.13,
      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
    },
    "debtUSD": {
      "statementPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
      "transferAmount": 0.0,
      "statementDebt": 0.0,
      "minPayment": 0.0,
      "remainingDebt": 0.0,
      "remainingMinPayment": 0.0,
      "currentPeriodExpense": 0.0,
      "totalDebt": 0.0,
      "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "NO_DEBT",
      "remainAutomaticPaymentAmount": 0.0
    },
    "debtEUR": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
    "debtGBP": { "...": "same fields as debtUSD" },
    "statementPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
    "totalDebtPaymentStatus": "HAS_DEBT",
    "automaticPaymentFlag": "N"
  },
  "result": { "returnCode": "1", "...": "" }
}
```

Field notes (my understanding from the card team, Selin please correct me if the business meaning is different):

- `statementDate` / `lastPayDate`: the last issued statement and its due date. `nextStatementDate` / `nextLastPayDate`: the coming ones.
- One block per currency: `debtTL`, `debtUSD`, `debtEUR`, `debtGBP`. **A block can be missing** (some cards have no GBP block at all). Missing block is not the same as a block with `NO_DEBT`; don't invent zeros for it.
- In each block: `statementDebt` is the statement debt, `minPayment` the minimum payment on the statement; `remainingDebt` / `remainingMinPayment` what is left of those after payments made since; `totalDebt` includes spending after the statement; `currentPeriodExpense` that spending; `transferAmount` carried over from the previous period.
- `statementPaymentStatus` / `totalDebtPaymentStatus`: `"HAS_DEBT"` or `"NO_DEBT"`, per block and once more at the top level for the card overall.
- `totalDebt` can be negative (credit balance on that currency). Status is `NO_DEBT` then.
- `automaticPaymentFlag`: `"Y"` / `"N"`. `remainAutomaticPaymentAmount` is only meaningful when it's `"Y"`.
- Heads-up: the `cardNumber` in this answer is masked differently from the card list (first 4 + last 4, `5400********1234`). Don't use it to match against the list; use `cardNumberLast4` or just keep the number you sent.

Errors: 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` (empty card number), 404 `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120`, 500 `FBE00099`. Example 404:

```json
    "details": { "guid": "<trace id>", "rootCause": "NotFoundException", "errorOrigin": "<gateway>" }
  }
}
```

(The message text here is just my example; only the code matters.)

[00:10:47] Selin Aydın: Okay. "Sizi ana menüye aktarıyorum." for non-Turkish. Writing.

[00:11:28] Kerem Yalçın: I like that. Selin?
[00:11:30] Selin Aydın: Yes, I'm okay. What is the sentence exactly?
[00:11:33] Ozan Er: We had something like "Bu konuda size yardımcı olamıyorum, ana menüye..." uh, I don't remember our wording.
[00:11:39] Kerem Yalçın: Let's make it consistent with the one we just wrote. "Size şu anda yardımcı olamıyorum" style.
[00:11:45] Selin Aydın: So: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?"
[00:11:51] Burcu Tan: Yes, that sounds natural.
[00:11:53] Kerem Yalçın: Good. Keep it.
[00:11:55] Deniz Arı: And if the answer to that question is unclear? Like they say "hmm, well, I don't know"?
[00:12:00] Selin Aydın: Same as every other question. Ask again, three tries.

[00:12:07] Selin Aydın: Yes.
[00:12:08] Ozan Er: Good, I'm writing it in our sheet. Out of scope: "Size bu konuda yardımcı olamıyorum. Sizi ana menüye aktarmamı ister misiniz?" Yes, main menu. Continue, back to flow. Unclear, ask again, three tries.

[00:12:27] Deniz Arı: Yes, yes, payment is separate. Payment and disputes go to an agent. This is only for things that have nothing to do with the statement.
[00:12:33] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Just so it's clear.
[00:12:35] Selin Aydın: Next, the angry customer. In the document: one calming reply, then agent.
[00:12:41] Kerem Yalçın: Yes, that's fine I think. We don't want the bot arguing with an angry customer.
[00:12:46] Deniz Arı: Okay. One calming sentence and then "Sizi müşteri temsilcimize aktarıyorum."
[00:12:51] Ozan Er: And insults, we don't answer the insult itself, right? It just stays polite.

[00:16:12] Burcu Tan: Yes, that's fine. Better than ours actually.
[00:16:15] Elçin Ural: Fine for me.
[00:16:16] Kerem Yalçın: Okay. Decided. Three silences: first two short repeat, third "Sesinizi alamadığım için görüşmeyi sonlandırıyorum." and hang up. Not main menu.

[00:17:31] Elçin Ural: Yes. Everywhere it speaks.

[00:17:43] Elçin Ural: İngiliz Sterlini, yes.

[00:17:53] Selin Aydın: [laughs] Still, I'll fix it.

1	# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt
2	
3	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.
4	
5	## When
6	
7	The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).
8	
9	## The scenario
10	
11	Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.
12	
13	In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.
14	
15	The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.
16	
17	## What you build
18	
19	1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
20	2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.
21	
22	Every call gives the phone agent two variables:
23	
24	- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
25	- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.
26	
27	## Inputs
28	
29	- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
30	- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
31	- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between the bank and our team, with the bank's analysis documents in `attachments/`.
32	- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
33	- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
34	- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve.
35	- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
36	- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

38	## How you are scored
39	
40	Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

67	# Credit cards: statements and payments
68	
69	Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.
70	
71	---
72	
73	**When will I get my statement?**
74	
75	Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.
76	
77	**Can I change my statement date?**
78	
79	Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.
80	
81	**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**
82	
83	Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.
84	
85	**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**
86	
87	First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.
88	
89	**What is the minimum payment?**
90	
91	It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.
92	
93	**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**
94	
95	Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.
96	
97	**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**
98	
99	Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.
100	
101	**When is my payment due?**
102	
103	Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.
104	
105	**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**
106	
107	Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.
108	
109	**How can I pay my card?**
110	
111	- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
112	- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
113	- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
114	- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.
115	
116	Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)
117	
118	**Can I pay my card over the phone?**
119	
120	You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.
121	
122	**Can I split my statement into instalments?**
123	
124	For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.
125	
126	**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**
127	
128	Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.
129	
130	**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**
131	
132	If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.
133

201	# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract
202	
203	Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
204	Date: 1 October 2026
205	Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)
206	
207	> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.
208	
209	## 1. Before you start
210	
211	- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
212	- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
213	- Base address for all seven:
214	
215	```
216	https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
217	```
218	
219	  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
220	- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
221	- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).
222	
223	## 2. Access token
224	
225	The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.
226	
227	```
228	POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
229	Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
230	
231	grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
232	```
233	
234	Answer:
235	
236	```json
237	{
238	  "access_token": "<token>",
239	  "token_type": "Bearer",
240	  "expires_in": 1800
241	}
242	```
243	
244	Then on every service call:
245	
246	| Header | Value |
247	|---|---|
248	| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
249	| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
250	| `Accept` | `application/json` |
251	
252	The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.
253	
254	(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)
255	
256	## 3. Envelope
257	
258	### Request
259	
260	```json
261	{
262	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
263	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
264	}
265	```
266	
267	`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.
268	
269	### Response
270	
271	Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.
272	
273	```json
274	{
275	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
276	  "result": {
277	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
278	    "returnCode": "1",
279	    "messageText": "Success",
280	    "code": "1",
281	    "message": "Success",
282	    "type": null,
283	    "details": {
284	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
285	      "rootCause": null,
286	      "errorOrigin": null
287	    }
288	  }
289	}
290	```
291	
292	Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.
293	
294	## 4. Errors
295	
296	Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:
297	
298	```json
299	{
300	  "result": {
301	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
302	    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
303	    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
304	    "code": "FBE00099",
305	    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
306	    "type": "ERROR",
307	    "details": {
308	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
309	      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
310	      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
311	    }
312	  }
313	}
314	```
315	
316	`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.
317	
318	Codes you can get:
319	
320	| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
321	|---|---|---|---|---|
322	| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
323	| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
324	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
325	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
326	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
327	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
328	| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |
329	
330	Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.
331	
332	Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.
333	
334	## 5. Services
335	
336	| # | Service | Called with | Gives back |
337	|---|---|---|---|
338	| 5.1 | `cards.list` | customer number | the customer's cards the assistant may talk about |
339	| 5.2 | `cards.balance` | card number | statement and due dates, debt per currency |
340	| 5.3 | `statement.week.get` | card number | the card's current statement week and day, joint statement info |
341	| 5.4 | `statement.week.decide` | card number + requested week | what the dates *would* be with that week (does not change anything) |
342	| 5.5 | `statement.week.change` | card number + requested week | changes the statement week |
343	| 5.6 | `contact.email.get` | customer number | registered e-mail / phone |
344	| 5.7 | `statement.pdf.send` | customer, card, currency, statement date, address | sends the statement PDF by e-mail |
345	
346	Card number: always send the `cardNumber` **exactly as `cards.list` returned it**. Don't rebuild it from digits the caller says.
347	
348	### 5.1 `cards.list`
349	
350	Request:
351	
352	```json
353	{
354	  "data": { "customerNo": "90000001", "aiFlow": "CardOps" },
355	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
356	}
357	```
358	
359	`customerNo` may be sent as a string or as a number, both are accepted. `aiFlow` tells us which use case is asking; for this one it's `"CardOps"` (not validated in test).
360	
361	Response, one card:
362	
363	```json
364	{
365	  "data": {
366	    "cards": [
367	      {
368	        "cardNumber": "540000******1234",
369	        "cardNumberLast4": "1234",
370	        "productName": "Yıldız Pratik Classic",
371	        "status": "A",
372	        "isMainCard": true
373	      }
374	    ],
375	    "validCardsCount": 1,

467	- `statementDate` / `lastPayDate`: the last issued statement and its due date. `nextStatementDate` / `nextLastPayDate`: the coming ones.

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between the bank and our team, with the bank's analysis documents in `attachments/`.
- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

## What you submit

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

```json
{
  "team": "Your team name",
  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
  "commit": "the commit you ran",
  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
  "trace": "traces/final.log",
  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
}
```

E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

# Credit cards: statements and payments

Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.

---

**When will I get my statement?**

Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.

**Can I change my statement date?**

Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.

**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**

Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.

**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**

First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.

**What is the minimum payment?**

It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.

**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**

Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.

**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**

Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.

**When is my payment due?**

Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.

**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**

Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.

**How can I pay my card?**

- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.

Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)

**Can I pay my card over the phone?**

You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.

**Can I split my statement into instalments?**

For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.

**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**

Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.

**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**

If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.

---

# IVR prompt sheet: debt inquiry and statement week change

Burcu Tan, IVR operations, 10 Sep 2026

Selin asked for "whatever the menu says today" before the kickoff, so here it is. I copied these out of the prompt list in our IVR designer this morning, card self-service branch, debt inquiry and statement week nodes only. Variable names are the ones the TTS template uses, not the service fields. Amounts and dates go through the number-to-speech module; everything else is recorded or plain TTS.

I haven't cleaned it up much. Some of these were written years ago and nobody has touched them since, so please don't read them as "how it should be". Questions to me, wording questions to Kerem.

## Debt inquiry

| Prompt id | When it plays | Turkish line | Variables |
|---|---|---|---|
| DBT-010 | Card has no unpaid statement debt | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınızda ödenmemiş bir borç görünmüyor. Bir sonraki ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| DBT-020 | Opening of the debt reading, before the per-currency lines | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız için bilgiler şöyle: | last4, card_name |
| DBT-031 | TL debt, caller has paid nothing yet | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası; yapmanız gereken en düşük ödeme {tl_min} Türk Lirası. | tl_total, tl_min |
| DBT-032 | TL debt, caller paid the minimum or more | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası, geriye kalan borcunuz {tl_remaining} Türk Lirası. Asgari ödemenizi yaptınız, teşekkür ederiz. | tl_total, tl_remaining |
| DBT-033 | TL debt, caller paid something but less than the minimum | Türk Lirası cinsinden toplam borcunuz {tl_total} Türk Lirası, yapmanız gereken en düşük ödeme {tl_min} Türk Lirası. Geriye kalan borcunuz {tl_remaining} Türk Lirası, ödemeniz gereken kalan asgari tutar ise {tl_remaining_min} Türk Lirası. | tl_total, tl_min, tl_remaining, tl_remaining_min |
| DBT-040 | Dollar debt (own sentence, plays after the TL line) | Dolar cinsinden toplam borcunuz {usd_total} USD, geriye kalan borcunuz {usd_remaining} USD, en düşük ödeme tutarı {usd_min} USD. | usd_total, usd_remaining, usd_min |
| DBT-041 | Euro debt (own sentence, plays after the dollar line) | Euro cinsinden toplam borcunuz {eur_total} Euro, geriye kalan borcunuz {eur_remaining} Euro, en düşük ödeme tutarı {eur_min} Euro. | eur_total, eur_remaining, eur_min |
| DBT-051 | No debt in TL | Türk Lirası cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-052 | No debt in dollar | Dolar cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-053 | No debt in euro | Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-054 | No debt in TL and dollar | Türk Lirası ve Dolar cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-055 | No debt in TL and euro | Türk Lirası ve Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-056 | No debt in dollar and euro | Dolar ve Euro cinsinden bir borcunuz yok. | none |
| DBT-060 | After the currency lines | Tüm borçlarınız için son ödeme gününüz {due_date}. | due_date |
| DBT-071 | After the debt info, debt or no debt: overall TL total | Bekleyen provizyonlar, faiz ve masraflar hesaba katılmadan kartınızın toplam Türk Lirası borcu {tl_overall} Türk Lirası. | tl_overall |
| DBT-072 | Same, overall dollar total | Bekleyen provizyonlar, faiz ve masraflar hesaba katılmadan toplam dolar borcu {usd_overall} dolar. | usd_overall |

Ops notes, debt inquiry:
- The three TL lines are picked by the IVR from the paid amount vs. the minimum. Ask Mert for the exact comparison, I only know it works.
- Dollar and euro are separate prompts on purpose; the recording studio would not do one sentence with two slots. "USD" is read out by the TTS as written. Yes, people have complained.
- There is no Sterling prompt at all. Never came up on the menu.
- The script I was handed in 2023 had the dollar total line (DBT-072) written twice and no euro total line. We recorded it once. So no euro total plays today.
- DBT-051 to DBT-056 cover only six combinations. If a card has no debt in any currency it goes to DBT-010 and never reaches these.

## Statement week change

| Prompt id | When it plays | Turkish line | Variables |
|---|---|---|---|
| STW-010 | Current payment week, ordinary card (after statement.week.get) | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına ayarlı. Önümüzdeki dönemde ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, week_ordinal, next_cut_date, next_due_date |

Önümüzdeki dönemde ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, linked_card_name, week_ordinal, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| STW-012 | Current payment week, the linked card itself (caller holds the card that hangs off a main card) | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız ile bu kartın bağlı olduğu {main_card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına ayarlı. Önümüzdeki dönemde ekstreniz {next_cut_date} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {next_due_date} olacak. | last4, card_name, main_card_name, week_ordinal, next_cut_date, next_due_date |
| STW-020 | Caller picked a week; IVR reads what the change will mean (after statement.week.decide) | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alınacak. Bundan sonra ekstreniz {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | last4, card_name, week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-021 | Same, card with a linked card | Son dört hanesi {last4} olan {card_name} kartınız ile buna bağlı {linked_card_name} kartınızın ödeme günü her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alınacak. Bundan sonra ekstreniz {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | last4, card_name, linked_card_name, week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-030 | Right after STW-020 / STW-021 | Bu değişikliği onaylar mısınız? | none |
| STW-040 | Caller confirmed and statement.week.change succeeded | Onayınızla ödeme gününüz her ayın {week_ordinal} haftasına alındı. Ekstreniz artık {cut_date_after} tarihinde kesilecek, son ödeme gününüz {due_date_after} olacak. | week_ordinal, cut_date_after, due_date_after |
| STW-091 | statement.week.change refuses: already changed this month | Ekstre tarihinizi değiştiremedik. Ekstre tarihi ayda yalnızca bir kez değiştirilebiliyor. | none |
| STW-092 | statement.week.change refuses: yearly limit reached | Ekstre tarihinizi değiştiremedik. Ekstre tarihi yılda en çok üç kez değiştirilebiliyor. | none |

Ops notes, statement week:
- week_ordinal is a word ("birinci", "ikinci" ...), not a number. The TTS says "1." badly.
- There is no linked-card variant of STW-020 for the case where the caller holds the linked card. It falls back to STW-021 with the names swapped, which sounds slightly off. Known.
- STW-091 and STW-092 only play after the caller has already confirmed, because we only find out from the change call. Callers find that annoying ("why did you ask me then"). I don't know of a way to check before; maybe Mert does.
- The limits in STW-091/092 are what the card system answered when these were recorded. I have not checked them against the product side recently, Kerem would know.
